title: Natural Domain and Range of a Quadratic Polynomial
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the natural domain and resulting range of the real-valued function defined by the formula f(x) = 1 + x^2.

steps.title: Analyze Algebraic Domain Restrictions
steps.explanation: Inspect the formula f(x) = 1 + x^2 for potential algebraic singularities, such as denominators that could equal zero or even roots of negative numbers.
steps.why: The natural domain consists of all real numbers for which the algebraic operations in the expression yield well-defined real numbers.

steps.title: Establish the Domain
steps.explanation: Since squaring any real number and adding 1 is valid for all real numbers without restriction, the function is defined on the entire real line.
steps.why: Polynomial functions are continuous and well-defined across all real numbers.

steps.title: Analyze Output Values for Range
steps.explanation: For every real number x, the square x^2 is non-negative (x^2 >= 0). Adding 1 gives 1 + x^2 >= 1. The minimum output occurs at x = 0, giving f(0) = 1, and as x approaches positive or negative infinity, 1 + x^2 grows without bound.
steps.why: The square of any real number is non-negative, bounding the upward-opening parabola from below at its vertex.

steps.title: State the Range
steps.explanation: Since the function is continuous on R and attains all values greater than or equal to 1, the range in interval notation is [1, inf).
steps.why: Continuous functions map connected intervals to connected intervals by the Intermediate Value Theorem.
